title: Revit 2026 STALE BUILD warning never clears: the opted-in Drafter manifest loads (and locks) the bridge DLL before the loader syncs
symptom: Revit's KOR tools work normally but the stale-build warning never clears: C:\ProgramData\KOR\logs\KOR-<date>.log logs "STALE BUILD: running '<old stamp>' but the share has '<new stamp>'. Close ALL Revit 2026 windows and relaunch - the update retries at startup" on every single launch, and following that instruction can never clear it.
cause: In %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>, KOR.Drafter.addin sorts before KOR.RevitTools.addin and Revit loads add-ins in that order. The Drafter manifest points at %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\<year>\KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll - a file inside the loader's own cache - so Revit has loaded and locked it before the loader's sync runs, and the loader's copy fails with "being used by another process". Since version.txt is stamped only if EVERY file copied, the stamp stays old permanently. Only a year opted in via build\Install-BridgeManifest.ps1 is affected. (A second Revit window of the same year causes a TRANSIENT form of the same lock on machines not opted in: card 36.)
check: C:\ProgramData\KOR\logs\loader.log - look for "copy skipped for KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll" followed by "cache NOT stamped current". Then compare %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\<year>\version.txt against <share>\current\<year>\version.txt, where the share root is the one line in kor-deploy.path beside the loader DLL (currently \\Kor-fs01\Drafting\KOR-Deploy). Affected = a machine whose %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>\KOR.Drafter.addin points into %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\. Fleet sweep for this: Operations tools/NetworkOpsMaint/revit-cache-state.ps1 (read-only, every profile and year). 27 Oct sweep: 1 of 31 machines read is opted in (KOR-302N 2026). Verified NOT opted in on 2026-10-27: KOR-307-N (3 of 3 manifests point at %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR.Drafter\<year>) and KOR-306 (2 of 2) - Revit Fleet actions 11491/11497/11498, NetworkOps reads 11478/11495.
fix: NOT YET SHIPPED. Approved by Ian at 22:46 on 2026-10-27, tracked as KorStandards.oversight commitment 65, owner Revit Fleet: a versioned bridge folder so a running Revit never holds the file being replaced; stamping that does not freeze on one locked file. (The per-machine installed-vs-share check is the sweep script named under check.) Revit Fleet sends the commit and version once proven on 302N; this card is amended then.
plain: Explains why Revit on 302N keeps saying its KOR tools are out of date even after a restart, and that the fix is approved but not built yet. Proof: KOR-302N 27 Oct, 7 of 7 Revit 2026 launches skipped the copy (10:35:25, 11:03:22, 11:08:31, 13:29:20, 13:31:38, 22:22:56, 22:45:38; actions 11450/11451); control Revit 2024 13:37:02 synced with no skip; cache vs share 8 of 10 identical by hash, only KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll + version.txt differ (11449); exclusive open succeeds with Revit closed (11454).
